clue.text: Printed details of meeting Queen perhaps needing new introduction

indicators.note: the phrase asks for the opening letter of the card term to be swapped for a different one

parts.note: a queen is one example of a face card, alongside king and jack

explanation.surface: A monarch, it seems, wants a fresh opening for some printed account of a meeting with her.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Queen perhaps' is not royalty but a playing card: FACE CARD. 'needing new introduction' replaces its first letter F with R.
explanation.definitionFit: At a horse-race meeting the printed programme listing runners and riders is the racecard.

clue.text: Runs rings round strutting chief, largely in extravagant style

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

indicators.note: the two rings go around the trimmed bird

parts.note: rings are O shapes, so two Os

indicators.note: largely means most of, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a cock struts and is cock of the walk, the chief

explanation.surface: Someone runs circles round a swaggering boss in a showy manner.
explanation.definitionFit: Rococo is an ornate eighteenth-century style, extravagant in decoration.

clue.text: John put an end to dance

parts.note: john and can are both slang for a toilet
to can something is to stop or scrap it

explanation.surface: John brought a stop to the dancing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'John' looks like a man's name; it is American slang for a toilet, like can.
explanation.definitionFit: The cancan is a high-kicking French music-hall dance.

clue.text: Oral language examination

indicators.note: oral means spoken, so the word is as it sounds

parts.note: Czech is a Slavic language

explanation.surface: A spoken language test.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oral language examination' reads as one test; split it into homophone indicator, the word said, and definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A check is an inspection or examination of something.

clue.text: Once more affirm right over property

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits over the second

parts.note: an estate is landed property

explanation.surface: A claimant reasserts their right to an estate.
explanation.definitionFit: To restate is to state again, affirming a point a second time.

clue.text: The Sun was responsible for his fall from elevated position

definitions.text: The Sun was responsible for his fall from elevated position

parts.words: The Sun was responsible for his fall from elevated position
parts.note: in Greek myth the boy flew too high on wax wings, the sun melted them and he fell into the sea

explanation.surface: A tabloid newspaper brought down someone in high office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Sun' reads like the British tabloid ruining a career; it is the literal sun of the myth.
explanation.definitionFit: Mythological figure whose waxen wings melted when he flew near the sun, so he plunged from the sky.

clue.text: Woman trains regularly, with husband imprisoned for fraud

indicators.note: the husband is locked inside the woman's name

parts.note: Carla is a woman's name

indicators.note: taking every other letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A woman keeps fit with training while her husband is jailed for fraud.
explanation.definitionFit: A charlatan is an impostor or quack, a fraud in human form.

clue.text: Extremely choppy at sea: huge storm that's unending

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so the letters are jumbled
having no end, so the last letter is dropped

explanation.surface: A huge, endless storm makes the sea very rough.
explanation.walkthrough: STORM loses its end to give STOR, which with HUGE is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Roughest is the superlative of rough, describing the most turbulent water.

clue.text: One who lived long ago raised northern songbirds?

indicators.note: lifted up, so in a down entry the letters run bottom to top

parts.note: split as song plus birds: an air is a song, emus are birds

explanation.surface: Northern songbirds are bred and raised, says the ornithologist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'songbirds?' splits into AIR and EMUS; the question mark warns emus cannot sing. N AIR EMUS read upwards gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sumerians were an ancient people of southern Mesopotamia.

clue.text: Discuss résumé covering Old Norse language

indicators.note: the résumé abbreviation wraps around the Old Norse abbreviation

parts.note: a résumé is a CV, curriculum vitae
Erse is an old name for Gaelic, a crossword favourite

explanation.surface: Talking over a résumé that lists knowledge of Old Norse as a language.
explanation.definitionFit: To converse is to talk together, a verb synonym for discussing.

clue.text: Vile allegation circulates, upsetting United manager — for starters, there's nothing in it

indicators.note: starters are first courses, so the opening letters of the preceding six words are taken

parts.words: Vile allegation circulates, upsetting United manager

explanation.surface: A nasty rumour about a football club's manager does the rounds, though it is quite baseless.
explanation.walkthrough: The football surface (United, manager) hides an initial-letter clue; the dash leads to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A vacuum is a space that contains no matter at all, empty of everything.

clue.text: One clergyman or another eschewing company

indicators.note: avoiding, so the company letters are removed

parts.note: another clergyman, a deacon

explanation.surface: One cleric or another avoids company.
explanation.definitionFit: A dean is a senior cleric heading a cathedral chapter.

clue.text: Eccentric patient finds housing in automobile

parts.note: an eccentric person is a crank
a doctor may call a patient a case

explanation.surface: An odd hospital patient ends up living in a car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'housing' looks like accommodation for the patient; it is a casing in a car engine.
explanation.definitionFit: The crankcase is the metal casing enclosing a car engine's crankshaft.

clue.text: He scored half-century, getting attention around close of match

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty

indicators.note: the word for attention wraps round the final letter of match

parts.note: to give an ear is to pay attention

indicators.note: the close of something is its end, so the final letter

explanation.surface: A cricketer makes fifty and draws notice as the game ends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'He scored half-century' reads as cricket; 'scored' means wrote music. Franz Lehár composed The Merry Widow.
explanation.definitionFit: Franz Lehár was a composer of operettas, so he scored, or wrote, music.

clue.text: Without coat, appear to be cold in store

indicators.note: removing the coat strips off the outermost letters at each end

parts.note: someone who shivers looks cold

explanation.surface: Without a coat, someone looks chilly in a shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'store' looks like a shop; it is a verb, to hoard. SHIVER loses its outer S and R.
explanation.definitionFit: To hive things away is to store them up, as bees do honey.

clue.text: Plead for season with crop yield

indicators.note: cropping cuts off the top, so the first letter goes

parts.note: winter is a season
to cede is to yield

explanation.surface: A farmer begs for a season of good harvest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crop' and 'yield' suggest farming; here crop means cut short.
explanation.definitionFit: To intercede for someone is to plead on their behalf.

clue.text: Not married, Samantha IS free woman

indicators.note: letters set free can be rearranged in any order
M is the abbreviation for married, so that letter is taken away

explanation.surface: An unmarried Samantha is free, says a claim about her status.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove M from SAMANTHA to leave SAANTHA, which 'free' rearranges; 'IS' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Natasha is a female given name, so it stands for a woman.

clue.text: Window cleaner gets to look around best part of royal dwelling at last

indicators.note: the looking word goes round the rest

parts.note: to see is to look

indicators.note: most of, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a queen is a royal

indicators.note: at last means finally, so only the closing letter of the word dwelling is used

explanation.surface: A window cleaner gets to inspect the finest part of a royal palace at last.
explanation.definitionFit: A squeegee is a rubber-bladed tool for wiping water off windows.

clue.text: Last one month, struggling to keep daughter and son apart

indicators.note: keeping something means holding it inside, so the scrambled letters hold the children
apart says the two inserted letters go in at separate places, not together
struggling letters are in disarray, rearranged

parts.note: one is I, the Roman numeral, followed by the word month as written

explanation.surface: Coming last for a month, a parent struggles to keep their two children apart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'struggling' rearranges I and MONTH into HINMOT; 'to keep' and 'apart' place D and S inside it at separate spots.
explanation.definitionFit: Hindmost means furthest behind, the very last one.

clue.text: With injection of drug, stop American passing away

indicators.note: an injection puts something inside, so one piece goes into another

parts.note: to quit is to stop
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Someone gives up a drug habit, involving an American who dies.
explanation.definitionFit: Quietus is a literary word for death or release from life.

clue.text: Hiding in drinks cabinet, he refuses to come out

indicators.note: the letters lie concealed in the words that follow

explanation.surface: A man hides in the drinks cabinet and will not come out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'come out' suggests leaving a hiding place; it means going on strike. A scab works during a strike.
explanation.definitionFit: A scab is a strike-breaker who refuses to join a walkout.

clue.text: Dressing gown at last is found in René's sack

indicators.note: one piece is found inside the other

parts.note: sack is slang for bed, and the French for bed is lit, a Frenchman's word

indicators.note: at last means finally, so only the closing letter of the word gown is used

explanation.surface: A dressing gown is finally discovered in a Frenchman's sack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dressing gown' looks like one item; split it: 'Dressing' is the definition and 'gown at last' gives N.
explanation.definitionFit: Lint is a soft fabric used as a wound dressing.

clue.text: Descriptive of pride one developed in ancestry?

indicators.note: the scrambled piece goes inside the ancestry word

parts.note: a line is a line of descent, ancestry

indicators.note: developed means evolved into a new form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Is pride a quality that developed in our ancestry?
explanation.walkthrough: 'pride' looks like the emotion; it is a group of lions, and 'Descriptive of' makes the definition an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Leonine means lion-like, and a pride is a group of lions.

clue.text: Judge's refusal to break almost backfired

indicators.note: fired backwards, so the pair is read in reverse

parts.note: no is a refusal

indicators.note: almost all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: to smash is to break

explanation.surface: A judge's refusal to break up nearly backfired on him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Judge' suggests a court; it is one of the Judges of Israel in the Bible. NO plus SMAS read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Samson was one of the Hebrew judges in the biblical Book of Judges.

clue.text: Some may arrive late to this meeting, from which a scene could result

definitions.text: Some may arrive late to this meeting

indicators.note: the letters could result in a new word if rearranged

explanation.surface: Latecomers arrive at a meeting that could cause a scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'late' looks like tardy; it means dead. The departed are said to visit a seance.
explanation.definitionFit: At a seance spirits of the dead, the late, are supposedly summoned to attend.

clue.text: Ancestor, one with roots

definitions.meaning: a tree of the genus Sambucus, which has roots

explanation.definitionFit: An elder is a senior forebear, and the elder is also a shrub or small tree.

clue.text: After a fight, force champion to have complete change of attitude

parts.note: a boxing bout is a fight
F is the physics symbol for force
an ace is a top performer

explanation.surface: After a scrap, a boxer forces the title-holder into a total reversal of views.
explanation.definitionFit: An about-face is a complete reversal of opinion, from the military turn-around order.

clue.text: The best street map is a valuable item

parts.note: top means the best
the A-Z is a well-known British street atlas, especially of London

explanation.surface: The finest street map is a precious possession.
explanation.walkthrough: The A to Z is a British street atlas, the standard London street guide.
explanation.definitionFit: Topaz is a gemstone, a precious and valuable item.

clue.text: Threatening look from firefly?

definitions.meaning: a firefly is something that glows, so whimsically a thing that glows

explanation.definitionFit: To glower is to scowl angrily, and fancifully a light-emitting insect is one that glows.

clue.text: Stop working after energy relief gets withdrawn

indicators.note: the working piece is placed after the reversed pair
drawn back, so the energy-and-relief pair is read in reverse order of letters

parts.note: sap means vigour or energy
aid is relief or help
on means working or operating

explanation.surface: Stop working once energy subsidies are taken away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stop' looks like a verb; it is an organ stop. 'gets withdrawn' reverses SAPAID to DIAPAS.
explanation.definitionFit: A diapason is a principal organ stop giving the instrument's main tone.

clue.text: Book's tense, set in Surrey town

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: Esher is a town in Surrey, a county south-west of London
T is a grammar abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: A novel's tense, a story set in a Surrey town.
explanation.walkthrough: Esher is a commuter town in Surrey, the English county just south-west of London.
explanation.definitionFit: Esther is a book of the Old Testament, named after its Jewish queen.

clue.text: Cézanne painting's heading off for port

indicators.note: the heading of a word is its opening letter
off means wrong or awry, so the letters are disordered

explanation.surface: A Cézanne painting has its title removed and is sent to a port.
explanation.walkthrough: PENZANCE is a port in Cornwall, England's south-west tip.
explanation.definitionFit: Penzance is a harbour town in Cornwall, a port on Mount's Bay.
